terms.gloss: The economics faculty of St Petersburg State University, where Durov is flyering.
terms.why_hard: Casual abbreviation must be kept casual, not expanded to a formal full name.

terms.gloss: Russian university student ID card, checked by door staff.
terms.why_hard: Translators may render as 'student pass', losing the Soviet-era artifact flavor.

terms.gloss: Philology student / philology faculty; Durov's own faculty at SPbGU.
terms.why_hard: Recurring across the book; must be consistent and distinguish from экономфак.

proposed.zh: 语文系学生 / 语文系
proposed.ja: 文学部の学生 / 文学部

terms.gloss: The hall attendant/concierge guarding entry, a fixture of Russian institutions.
terms.why_hard: No exact English equivalent; 'security guard' overstates, 'doorman' misleads.

terms.gloss: St Petersburg bar named after Dostoevsky's novel The Idiot, expat hangout.
terms.why_hard: Allusion to Dostoevsky plus the expat-American clientele; both layers matter.

terms.gloss: Web metaphor: Durov sees students as 'traffic' (visitors/users) to be converted.
terms.why_hard: Recurring metaphor that frames the whole scene as site promotion; must keep the internet sense.

terms.gloss: Echo of 'making friends' social-network functionality ('connections').
terms.why_hard: Deliberate pun on site features vs real life; dropping it loses the joke.

proposed.ja: 現実でつながりを作る

terms.gloss: Russian-voiced paraphrase of Morpheus's speech to Neo in The Matrix (1999).
terms.why_hard: Unmarked Matrix quotation; a translator who doesn't catch it loses the framing device.

proposed.en: (Morpheus's Matrix speech: 'I know you're out there... a world without rules and controls, where anything is possible')
proposed.zh: （《黑客帝国》墨菲斯台词：“我知道你在这里……一个没有规则和控制的世界，在那里一切皆有可能”）
proposed.ja: （『マトリックス』のモーフィアスの台詞：「お前がそこにいるのは分かる……規則も支配もない、すべてが可能な世界を見せよう」）

terms.gloss: The spot where the campus crowd hangs out; slang 'тусовка' = scene/hangout.
terms.why_hard: Two slang words at once; literal 'trampled patch' would read as nonsense.

terms.gloss: Recruitment/intelligence metaphor: Durov treats flyering like agent recruitment.
terms.why_hard: Sustained spy register (вербовать, агенты влияния) that must be kept consistent.

proposed.ja: 我々は協力者をリクルートする

terms.gloss: Slang for the administration's poster-hangers / poster-cleanup crew.
terms.why_hard: Coinage; may be misread as 'posters' rather than the people who tear them down.

proposed.ja: ポスストーリの張り紙係

terms.gloss: The student web forum (spbgu.ru), Durov's first project, predecessor of VK.
terms.why_hard: Must not become generic 'forum discussion'; it's a specific website the passage promotes.

terms.gloss: 2000s 'glamour girl': designer-dressed, money-chasing stereotype.
terms.why_hard: Glamur was a loaded 2000s buzzword; needs period-appropriate pejorative.

terms.gloss: Clutch bag, marker of the glamour stereotype.
terms.why_hard: Minor, but signals the fashion typing Durov does.

terms.gloss: Slang: to snare/land a rich guy.
terms.why_hard: Coarse colloquial register must survive, not be sanitized.

terms.gloss: Slang: badmouthed, tore him apart (behind his back).
terms.why_hard: Literally 'smeared him along the wall'; a vivid vulgarism needing an equivalent idiom.

proposed.ja: さんざんこき下ろしていた

terms.gloss: Alternative/non-mainstream girl — subculture type, the opposite of glamour.
terms.why_hard: Untranslatable coinage; 2000s Russian youth typology of 'формал/неформал'.

proposed.ja: ノンコンフォrm（反体制系）の女子

terms.gloss: Slang: nerdy swot, grind (from 'botanist').
terms.why_hard: Must match register of campus stereotype; 'robot' is a false cognate trap.

terms.gloss: An intelligent-looking sort of guy.
terms.why_hard: Deliberately slovenly spoken register ('vredе tip') inside Durov's inner monologue.

proposed.ja: いかにもインテリ風のタイプ

terms.gloss: Software metaphor: run the acquaintance 'program' (scripted pick-up routine).
terms.why_hard: Part of the running code/software metaphor system in this passage; must stay computational.

proposed.ja: 知り合いのプログラムを起動する

terms.gloss: The philology faculty's famous inner courtyard, a campus institution.
terms.why_hard: Could be generic 'yard'; it's a specific storied hangout with the dean's sculptures.

terms.gloss: The philology dean (A. S. Gerd-era lore) known for collecting sculpture.
terms.why_hard: Real anecdote about a real dean; needs checking to name or keep anonymous.

proposed.ja: 学部長が彫刻を収集している

terms.gloss: Philologists' Day, an unofficial in-joke holiday at the faculty.
terms.why_hard: May read as a generic professional day; it's faculty lore.

terms.gloss: Dressed up in a powdered-age frock coat; dean's theatrical entrances.
terms.why_hard: ряженый implies fancy-dress costumery, not just clothing.

proposed.en: dressed up in a powdered wig and frock coat
proposed.ja: 十八世紀風の衣装に身を包んで

terms.gloss: Harley-Davidson motorcycle.
terms.why_hard: Transliteration must be recognized as a motorcycle brand.

terms.gloss: Deus ex machina — Latin theatrical trope, punning on the hot-air balloon arrival.
terms.why_hard: The balloon makes the pun literal; translator must keep the classical allusion and the joke.

terms.gloss: Trade-union committee (profsoyuzny komitet), campus power structure at Russian universities.
terms.why_hard: No target-culture analogue; needs a consistent institutional rendering across the book.

terms.gloss: The faculty's student opposition faction, part of campus politics.
terms.why_hard: Could be mistaken for national political opposition; context is faculty politics.

terms.gloss: The balance of forces / lay of the land in faculty politics.
terms.why_hard: Colloquial political idiom; must read as informal, not military.

terms.gloss: 'Agents of influence' — KGB term for opinion-formers, reused as Durov's spy metaphor.
terms.why_hard: Carries Soviet intelligence connotation; must retain the espionage echo.

proposed.zh: 意见领袖（影响力代理人）

terms.gloss: The little suitcase Durov carries posters in; salesman image.
terms.why_hard: Recurring prop; the diminutive makes him look harmless/solicitor-like.

terms.gloss: pseudo-values of consumer society, a staple phrase of Soviet moralising and countercultural critique
terms.why_hard: sounds like generic sociology unless translated with the intellectual, slightly self-righteous edge Durov intends

proposed.zh: 消费主义社会的虚假价值观
proposed.ja: 消費社会のまやかしの価値観

terms.gloss: kept my mind unpolluted/clear
terms.why_hard: translating literally as 'kept my head clean' loses the deliberate mental hygiene / anti-propaganda nuance

proposed.ja: 頭の中を澄んだ状態に保っていた

terms.gloss: software engineers/developers working on VKontakte
terms.why_hard: vague word that could mean generic product designers rather than coding engineers

terms.gloss: late-Soviet state kindergarten
terms.why_hard: carries institutional connotations of state regimentation, drabness, and administrative inertia

proposed.ja: ソ連末期の公立幼稚園

terms.gloss: formally registered under the propiska residential permit system
terms.why_hard: propiska is an administrative residency mandate tying individuals strictly to district services

proposed.ja: 住民登録（プロピスカ）が割り当てられて

terms.gloss: bowl of semolina porridge, the ubiquitous symbol of Soviet childhood misery and institutional feeding
